key_insight: Region-aware Mixture of Experts models reproduce much of the accuracy gained through data assimilation in an axial compressor without requiring experimental inputs during deployment.
engineering_relevance: Learned forcing terms offer a route to improving turbomachinery CFD predictions beyond baseline RANS using experimentally informed corrections.
method: Fuse experimental PIV with steady fixed-grid RANS and unsteady moving-grid hybrid RANS/LES using a Multi-Fidelity Ensemble Kalman Filter.
Train neural networks on the enriched database to map local velocity, velocity gradients and turbulent viscosity to discrete Navier–Stokes forcing terms.
Use a Mixture of Experts to combine learned corrections across different flow regions.
evidence_signal: Against experimental PIV, the Mixture of Experts yields systematically lower discrepancies than baseline RANS and results very similar to the assimilation solution.
watch_item: Individual neural models can exceed baseline RANS errors near blade tips; generalization beyond the studied compressor conditions is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Assisted Turbulence Modeling via Data Assimilation and Machine Learning for Turbomachinery Flows
